Full nine hours to pay back last night's shortfall; the LIS turn doesn't report until 15:25 local.
Sleep the normal night, then use the day off to start dragging bedtime earlier.
Lights out at 20:00 local on your day off — the only way to get a real sleep in front of an 05:40 report, and you'll have been up 12h30 so you will drop off.
Straight to bed after the four-sector FRA day; getting up at 06:00 local keeps the pressure building for tomorrow's very early night.
A proper siesta on the day off to bank an hour ahead of the 16h52 monster on the 7th.
Bed at 20:15 local — you need every minute of this before a 05:40 report that doesn't finish until 22:32.
Home at 23:30 local after nearly seventeen hours on duty; sleep as long as the body will take it.
Another 19:30 local bedtime on the day off to cover the 05:05 LIS report.
Awake since 03:05 local and finished by 10:19 — take a solid mid-morning sleep, it also lets you push tonight later.
Deliberately going to bed late and getting up at 10:00 local, because tomorrow you're airborne until 02:31 and blocking in at 03:01.
In the door at 03:55 local and asleep immediately, but keeping it to under six hours so you can get back down again this evening.
Second sleep of the day off — the only way to flip from a 03:01 finish to an 05:40 report in one calendar day.
Straight home from the FCO turn and 90 minutes down to clear the debt from the split night.
Back on a normal night to reset the body clock before the standby block.
An hour before the 14:00 standby opens, in case they call you out for something that finishes late.
Standby released at 20:00 local, so a straightforward full night.
Early to bed on the day off — you're contactable from 06:00 local and I'm assuming you may have to move to the airport.
This is the single most important sleep of the month: standby releases at 13:00 local and you report at 23:00 for an all-night ARN, so black out the room and treat this afternoon as your night.
Home by 10:00 local having flown straight through the window of circadian low — sleep now while the pressure is still there, and don't fight it awake.
Get one clean night in to pull the clock back to Madrid time after the night flight.
Day-off early night ahead of the 05:05 four-sector day.
Ten hours and a lie-in to 09:00 local — tomorrow you don't get to bed until nearly 06:00.
Nap before you leave for a 15:25 report that ends with a DUB night sector landing at 05:11 — go in with a full tank.
Home at 06:35 local off an all-nighter; sleep through the morning but get up early afternoon so tonight still works.
Full night on the day off to finish the recovery — the BCN turn isn't until midday.
Short BCN day means an early bed is achievable, and you need it for an 06:10 report into a 15h01 DUB double.
Home at 22:05 local after fifteen hours — bed straight away, no unwinding.
Day-off early night for the 05:05 FCO/FRA report.
Getting up at 06:30 local on the day off is deliberate — you need twelve hours of wakefulness to fall asleep at 18:30 tonight.
Bed at 18:30 local for the 04:35 report, the earliest of the month; alarm goes at 02:35 local so nothing later will do.
Forty-five minutes on getting home after fifteen hours awake, just enough to be safe and civil for the evening.
Long night to clear the debt — tomorrow is a late finish, not an early start.
An hour before the 14:40 report; the ARN return blocks in at 00:26 local.
In the door about 01:50 local — sleep now, but keep it to under seven hours so the evening sleep still comes.
Second sleep on the day off to get you round from a 00:56 finish to an 05:05 report.
Short nap after the FCO turn — you're up at 03:05 local again tomorrow and the evening bedtime is going to be a squeeze.
Back-to-back 05:05 reports, so bed at 20:00 local even if you're not tired — you've been awake since 03:05.
Last duty done by 10:07 local; sleep off the accumulated early starts before you do anything else.

raised.statement: A 16h52 duty, four sectors, starting at 05:40 local — you'll be awake from about 03:40 local until past midnight, roughly 21 hours, with the last sector landing at 22:02. No sleep plan makes that duty feel short.

Home standby 06:00-13:00 local, then report 23:00 local the same day for an all-night MAD-ARN-MAD finishing 09:10 the next morning. Only 10 hours between standby release and report, and the sleep you need in that gap is a daytime sleep after you've already been up since 04:30.
AU342 lands at 02:31 local and you're off duty at 03:01 — the whole last sector sits inside the 02:00-06:00 body-time trough after a 13h46 day.

You block in at 03:01 local on the 11th and report at 05:40 local on the 12th. The calendar shows a day off in between, but the body clock has to move about nine hours in one go — it can't, so the 11th has to be split into two sleeps.
Off duty 21:43 local on the 1st, report 07:45 local on the 2nd. With 55 minutes each way to MAD that's about 8h10 actually at home and realistically 6h30 in bed, in front of a 10h09 duty to ARN.
AU837 from DUB lands at 05:11 local after a 14h16 duty — approach and landing right at the bottom of the circadian dip, having been awake since about 12:00 the previous day.
An 04:35 local report means an alarm at about 02:35 and leaving home at 03:40. You cannot sleep enough before that no matter how early you go to bed, and it opens a 12h06 four-sector day.
05:05 local reports on both the 29th and the 30th, and the 29th only ends at 12:15 local — the second early start is flown on a night that starts at 20:00 with an alarm at 03:05.
Duty on the 27th ends 00:56 local on the 28th, then a 05:05 report on the 29th. The single day off has to absorb a late finish and set up an early start, which is two opposite demands.

The two SBY lines show a MAD-MAD sector and a duty window but do not say whether it is home standby or airport standby. I have planned for home standby with the option of getting to MAD, and I have taken the report time as the start of the window with no reporting offset applied.
AU596 appears twice with different routings (MAD-FCO on 12/09, ARN-MAD on 16/09), as do AU445, AU316 and AU690. I have read them exactly as printed, but it is worth a glance before the day.

15h01 across four sectors with an 06:10 local report, and the same pattern again on 05/09 (14h14), 19/09 (14h16) and 24/09 (14h16) — four duties over fourteen hours in the month, three of them off early reports.

blocks.why: Full night in your own bed before an easy 10:00 report — bank it, because the next 48 hours are all backside of the clock.
Straight to bed after the BCN turn: this five and a half hours is the only sleep you'll get before an 00:55 report, so blackout blinds and phone off.
Home by 09:25 off the Dublin night — get your head down immediately, before the morning light kills it, because you're back at report at 18:30.
In at 02:35 after the LHR night — sleep as long as your body lets you, first day off is for paying back the debt.
First proper normal night; start walking bedtime backwards now for the 06:10 report on the 7th.
An hour earlier again — the body clock only moves about an hour a day, so do it gradually.
23:00 to 07:00 local, one more step towards an early-start body clock.
Deliberate 21:00 bedtime on your last day off so the 04:20 alarm for a 06:10 report isn't a two-hour night.
Short kip after the Lisbon turn to take the edge off, and still leave you sleepy enough for a 20:30 bedtime.
Early to bed for the 05:40 report — tomorrow is a four-sector 12-hour day and this is all the sleep you get.
Home at 18:45 wrecked after four sectors; long sleep into the day off to clear the debt.
An early-afternoon hour so you can survive being awake until 20:00 and still hit the 04:35 report fresh-ish.
20:00 lights out on a day off — feels wrong, but a 04:35 report means the alarm goes at 02:45.
Nap on landing back from Frankfurt so you're not running on a six-hour night into a normal evening.
Longest night you can get before the 16-hour Stockholm day — this is the sleep that has to carry you to 06:51 tomorrow morning.
Compulsory pre-duty nap: you sign on at 14:40 and don't stop flying until sunrise, so bank two hours before you leave.
Straight to bed at 08:15 off the ARN night — sleep the morning, then get up so you can still sleep tonight for the sim.
Re-anchoring to a normal night ahead of an 08:00 sim start.
Long one after the sim — mentally that's as tiring as a four-sector day.
Normal night; four days off, so the job is to arrive at the 18th with zero sleep debt.
Start creeping bedtime earlier for the 05:05 report on the 18th.
22:00 to 06:00 — one more hour earlier, no lie-in, keep the pressure on.
Short afternoon top-up on the last day off, insurance in case tonight's early bedtime doesn't take.
20:15 bedtime for an 03:15 alarm — the 18th is a 17-hour day and you cannot start it short.
Home just before 23:00 after nearly 17 hours; take everything the clock allows before tomorrow's late finish.
Nap before signing on at 14:40 — you land at 04:13 tomorrow morning and you'll be flying the last sector through the worst hour of the night.
In the door at 05:40, sleep the morning off, then get up around midday so you can still sleep tonight.
Second sleep of the day off, aimed at putting a proper night behind you before another 02:55 finish.
Forty-five minutes before you leave for the 12:20 report — small, but it buys you the last two sectors.
Home at 03:50; sleep until mid-morning only, because tonight has to be an early night for a 04:35 report.
19:30 lights out after only nine hours awake — it will be a fight, but the 23rd is the longest duty of the month.
Nine hours after a 17-hour four-sector day; don't set an alarm any earlier than you have to.
Early night again for the 05:40 CDG report — short day tomorrow, so this is enough.
Nap on the way into three days off, then stay up for a normal bedtime and reset properly.
First full recovery night of the block — no alarm.
Normal night; the last two duties are afternoon reports so you can drift back to civilian hours.
Keep it regular — same time in, same time out.
Late report tomorrow at 15:25, so a normal night with a lie-in is exactly right.
Home around 23:45 from Frankfurt; sleep in, because tomorrow finishes at 03:22.
An hour down before the 13:15 report — the Rome sector lands at 02:52 and that hour is what keeps you sharp for it.
Straight to bed at 02:45 after the last sector of the month — nothing else in the diary, sleep it out.

raised.statement: The BCN day duty ends 14:54 local and you report again at 00:55 local — about 10 hours door-to-door, of which the commute takes nearly two, so the only sleep available is an evening nap.
MD882/MD826 (report 00:55, off blocks 07:58 local) sits entirely across 02:00–06:00 body time, with no acclimatisation credit and no prior night sleep.

You block in from the Dublin night at 07:58 local and report for the LHR duty at 18:30 the same day — roughly 10 hours at home, all of it in daylight, chasing sleep your body clock does not want to give.
16h11 duty, four sectors, report 14:40 and off duty 06:51 the next morning — the last sector ARN–MAD flies right through 02:00–06:00 body time at the end of a very long day.
The 12th is printed as LIB but you are on duty until 06:51 local that morning, so the day off is really a recovery day and gives you no useful rest credit.
Report 06:10 on the 7th then 05:40 on the 8th, and the 8th is a four-sector 12h07 duty — the sleep before it is capped at about seven hours no matter how well you plan it.
16h56 duty, four sectors, starting from an 05:05 report — the pre-duty sleep has to end at 03:15 local, which realistically means seven hours at best against a seventeen-hour day.
A 14h03 duty finishing at 04:43 local follows the 16h56 duty of the 18th with only about 16h39 between them — two WOCL-crossing days back to back with one short night in the middle.

You finish at 02:55 local on the 22nd and report at 04:35 local on the 23rd — about 25h40 apart — and the 23rd is a 17h02 four-sector duty, the longest of the month. The single day off cannot absorb that clock swing.
14h07 duty ending 03:22 local on 1 October, following the 29th which finished at 22:48 with about 14h27 rest — and the roster period ends mid-recovery, so nothing after it is visible.

The roster prints local time at each station and gives no UTC column, so every instant here is a conversion: MAD/BCN/FRA/CDG/ARN/FCO at UTC+2 and LHR/DUB/LIS at UTC+1 for all of September 2026. The 1h00 report offset and 0h30 post-flight duty end are inferred from the printed columns, not stated in the document.
